draft.shortGloss: to build; to construct; to wake someone up
draft.emotion: focused and industrious, intent on creating something lasting and solid
notes: Note the difference between 'membangun' (to build/construct) and 'membangunkan' (to wake someone up). Even though they share the same root, the suffix '-kan' is necessary for the transitive 'wake up' meaning.
When referring to abstract concepts, such as a business or a relationship, you can still use 'membangun' as in English 'building a career' or 'building trust'.

senses.definition: To make something by putting parts together, especially buildings or structures.

examples.text: Mereka sedang membangun rumah baru di dekat sungai.
examples.translation: They are building a new house near the river.
examples.emotion: informative and clear, describing a project underway

senses.definition: To cause someone to stop sleeping.

examples.text: Tolong bangunkan adik sebelum jam tujuh.
examples.translation: Please wake up your little brother before seven o'clock.
examples.emotion: gentle but firm, giving an instruction to someone else
examples.note: Note the change to 'bangunkan' for this specific transitive sense.
